description: The bar chart illustrates the Shapley values for three multilingual models—mBERT (light blue), XLM-R (dark blue), and chLSTM (light green)—across eight linguistic categories: L₄⁺, L₃, L₂, L₁, T, R₁, R₂, R₃, and R₄⁺, which likely represent different levels or types of morphosyntactic features or language groups. The vertical axis, labeled “Shapley value,” ranges from 0 to 80 with tick marks at intervals of 20, indicating the relative contribution of each model to explaining variance in the target task. The horizontal axis lists the categories in a left-to-right sequence that may reflect increasing complexity or a specific linguistic hierarchy. The tallest bars appear in the “T” category, where mBERT reaches approximately 60, XLM-R around 55, and chLSTM peaks at about 80, suggesting chLSTM has the highest explanatory power for this feature. In contrast, most other categories show much lower values, often below 15, with R₃ and R₄⁺ showing near-zero contributions across all models. The bars are grouped by category, with each model’s contribution shown as a separate adjacent bar, allowing direct comparison. No bars are shaded or emphasized beyond their color coding, and the chart does not include error bars or statistical annotations. The overall pattern suggests that the models differ significantly in their ability to capture certain linguistic features, with chLSTM outperforming the others in the “T” category while all models show minimal contribution in the R₃ and R₄⁺ categories.
